role: calibration only (discretised projection / Furstenberg-set statistics of solution directions)
missing_theorem: None for ES. Projection theorems need δ-discretised sets of size δ^{−s}; at one n there are ≍ polylog solutions, and over many n the statement is an average (B6). The directions concentrate near the axes anyway: every solution at a prime has z/x ≥ (3/4)√p (Q14 Z0954).

missing_theorem: For every prime p some (c,d) has a determinant-1 matrix with diagonal ≡ −1 (mod 4cd) and off-diagonal product 4c²dp (= ES, Type II). Spectral counting (Selberg 3/16, Kim–Sarnak 7/64) controls counts with |entries| ≤ T → ∞. The fixed product is a divisor split of one integer at a level tied to the solution.

role: effective ternary representation (Blomer–Harcos hybrid subconvexity) + 10^18 verification
missing_theorem: For every prime p > P₀ (P₀ ≤ 10^18), some ternary quadratic form attached to ES represents an integer attached to p in a way that yields a certificate. Ternary representation theorems (Duke–Schulze-Pillot, Blomer–Harcos) are genus/spinor-level and hold at odd squares, so they cannot produce Type I/II solutions (T1). ES also has no ternary quadratic reformulation with power-size representation counts.

role: ES₅ sign as a knot signature of the 2-bridge link b(p,A)
missing_theorem: No ES-yielding statement. The sign (A/p) is the linking-form class of Σ₂(b(p,A)) = L(p,A) (Q14 Z2800), but σ(b(p,A)) does not determine it: both symbols occur at σ = 0 (Pass 1 H04). Existence of a 3-vertex plumbing in the QNR class is ES₅.

role: Heegaard Floer d-invariants as a selector for 3-chain plumbings in the QNR class
missing_theorem: A closed-form test T(p), built from d(L(p,A), ·) data, such that T(p) holds iff some A with (A/p) = −1 has r(p/A) = 3, and T(p) holds for every prime. Every L(p,A) bounds its own negative-definite plumbing, so d-invariants obstruct other fillings, not the existence of A. The test would be ES₅ in disguise.

role: calibration: topological explanation of T1 via metabolic linking forms (Lisca)
missing_theorem: No ES yield. Calibration (PROVED, elementary): every linking form on ℤ/m² is metabolic, since λ(mx, mx) = A x² ∈ ℤ, so mℤ/m² is isotropic of order m. This is the topological face of T1, (A/m²) = 1 for all A prime to m. Lisca's rational-ball condition is strictly finer, since not every L(m², A) bounds a rational ball. At a prime p no linking form is metabolic, and that is all T1's absence says.
next: Close. Optionally note in T1_TEMPLATE: T1 ⟺ metabolic linking form, which is weaker than bounding a rational ball.

role: ES₅ as a Donaldson-style lattice-embedding question
missing_theorem: For every prime p some 3-chain lattice of determinant p with (A/p) = −1 exists (= ES₅). The proposed check, that the square class of the orthogonal complement in ℤ^k equals the ES sign, is a tautology of gluing (Nikulin). The complement of a determinant-p lattice in a unimodular lattice has anti-isometric discriminant form, whose class is (−1/p)(A/p) = (A/p) at p ≡ 1 (4).
note: The embedding computation would only confirm the gluing identity.

role: calibration only (Goeritz matrix of a 2-bridge diagram = chain matrix)
missing_theorem: None for ES. Calibration (standard): for an alternating 2-bridge diagram in plumbing form, the Goeritz matrix is the tridiagonal chain matrix up to sign/stabilisation (Gordon–Litherland). Knot tables then list the same (p, A) data.

role: ES₅ sign as a phase of WRT quantum invariants; sums over words
missing_theorem: No ES-yielding statement. Jeffrey's formula involves the Gauss sum G(A, p) = (A/p)G(1, p), so the Legendre symbol appears as a phase (calibration, true). Σ_{A∈L₃(p)} τ_r(L(p,A)) is a sum over a polylog set with no structure; its non-vanishing on QNR terms is ES₅.

missing_theorem: For every prime p some hyperbolic word matrix with (1,2)-entry p, length-3 cutting sequence and the character condition exists (= ES₅).
